title: Annual low-flow medians rose while June-November medians fell at 33 of 186 Canadian reference stations from 1975-1999 to 2000-2024
abstract: We tested whether annual low-flow medians show the same direction of change as June-November low-flow medians. We used the HYDAT release of 2026-10-19 and the 2020 Canadian reference network. We kept 186 stations with at least 20 complete years in each period, 1975-1999 and 2000-2024. A low flow is the smallest seven-day mean in the year or season. June-November medians fell at 102 stations. Annual medians rose at 33 of these stations, or 17.7% of the full sample. The conditional 95% block resampling range for this share was 9.1% to 28.1%. Fourteen stations had a June-November decrease of at least 10% and a rise in the annual median. Winter medians rose at 32 of the 33 stations. The national median summer change was small and uncertain. Among 91 stations with all 50 years complete, 20 had the direction mismatch and eight met the 10% rule. All 252 balanced assignments of ten five-year blocks gave upper-tail p values of 0.087 and 0.060. Thus the counts do not clearly exceed this stationary reference. The result gives a benchmark for the limits of annual indicators. It does not prove a physical regime change. Selected seasons, record coverage, dependent sites, and uncertain ice-affected flows limit the result. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, two figures, and an independent numerical check are included. External records stay outside the package.

display.caption: Annual and seasonal changes at 186 reference stations. Summer is June-November. Winter is December-May. Each low flow is the smallest seven-day mean. A shows station median symmetric changes with conditional 95% resampling ranges. B gives the four direction counts. The orange box marks summer declines with annual rises. C shows coarse 20-point bins; the displayed axes stop at 150 points. The complete bin table extends to 200 points.

The 91 stations with all 50 years complete had 20 direction mismatches and eight summer decreases of at least 10% with annual rises. Both counts were within the reference range from all 252 balanced assignments of ten five-year blocks. Upper-tail p values were 0.087 and 0.060. This check assumes that the five-year blocks are exchangeable under an unchanged regime. It was added after the primary point results were seen.

citations.reason: Prior campaign study uses the same HYDAT snapshot for a different river-ice question. It identified an existing shared source. We do not reuse its code or claim independent data confirmation.

Prior Canadian annual and seasonal low-flow study provides the season split and shows why annual indicators can miss seasonal change. We add a newer fixed-period count benchmark, not the first statement of this effect.
Prior British Columbia work studies summer minimum flow and climate drivers. Our descriptive count does not identify those drivers.
Prior European mixed-season frequency analysis gives context. We do not estimate design flows or return periods.
